- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts show gradual upward drift, correct for overconfidence by reducing slope slightly and adding a lagged mean reversion term.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 30d mean), model forecasts often overshoot; apply a 3-5 day decay filter to dampen momentum.
- In high-bearish sentiment (≥0.67) with net supply negative, model forecasts tend to underestimate true downside; add a 10-15% downward bias to forecast mean.
- When official event balance is heavily bearish (net supply < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model forecasts often lag; adjust by adding 1-2 days of lagged historical mean to forecast.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and low sentiment volatility, apply a smoothing filter to reduce noise; use 3-period moving average of recent 30d true values as baseline.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish spikes followed by bearish corrections, model tends to overreact; apply a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10-20% after 2 consecutive bullish days.
